chief_complaint: intense fear of public speaking and blushing
hpi_details: A 41-year-old male presents to the clinic with intense fear of public speaking and blushing. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks a glitch in his blood circulation makes all the blood rush to his face whenever people look at him.
concerns: He is worried that freezing up and turning crimson during an upcoming executive presentation will destroy his reputation and ruin his chance for a promotion.
expectations: He hopes to get a fast-acting tablet he can take before speaking engagements to prevent his face from flushing and his hands from shaking.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Social Anxiety Disorder evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Social Anxiety Disorder is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes cognitive behavioural therapy; a qualified prescriber may consider medication for performance-only or generalized symptoms after checking contraindications and interactions.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: A 41-year-old male presents to the clinic with intense fear of public speaking and blushing. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Social Anxiety Disorder.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Social Anxiety Disorder.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Offer cognitive behavioural therapy with graduated exposure.
A qualified prescriber may consider medication after assessing cardiovascular, respiratory, psychiatric, and drug-interaction risks.
Assess suicidal or homicidal ideation and arrange urgent psychiatric evaluation if there is imminent risk.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
